  \[ f^G \  \colon \ S^{U^G\oplus{\mathbb R}^{m+k}} =  (S^{U\oplus{\mathbb R}^{m+k}})^G\ \longrightarrow\  X(U\oplus{\mathbb R}^m)^G
    \ , \]
  the restriction to $G$-fixed points.
  As the integer $k$ varies, the geometric fixed point maps \eqref{eq:define_Phi^G_map}
  form a monoidal natural transformation $\Phi^G\colon \pi_*^G\longrightarrow\Phi^G_*$
  between lax symmetric monoidal functors that descend through $\gamma^\wedge_G$.
  So there is a unique monoidal natural transformation
  \[ \bar\Phi^G \ \colon \ \bar\pi_*^G \ \longrightarrow \ \bar\Phi^G_* \]
  of lax symmetric monoidal functors ${\mathcal S} p^\wedge_G\longrightarrow\operatorname{GrAb}^\otimes$
  such that $\bar\Phi^G\circ \gamma^\wedge_G=\Phi^G$.
<!-- end construction-20 -->
<!-- construction-21: body_md -->
A morphism $f\colon X\longrightarrow Y$ of orthogonal spectra is a {\em global equivalence}
  if the induced map of equivariant homotopy groups $\pi_k^G(f)\colon \pi_k^G(X)\longrightarrow\pi_k^G(Y)$
  is an isomorphism for all $k\in{\mathbb Z}$ and all compact Lie groups $G$.
  We show in \cite[Theorem 4.3.18]{schwede:global} that the global equivalences
  are part of a stable, cofibrantly generated, proper and topological model structure
  on the category of orthogonal spectra.
  By \cite[Proposition 4.3.24]{schwede:global},
  the smash product of orthogonal spectra is a Quillen bifunctor for the global model structure.
  Since the monoidal unit, the sphere spectrum ${\mathbb S}$, is cofibrant in the global model structure,
  we are dealing with a symmetric monoidal model category.
  The monoidal localization thus yields a symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category
  \[ {\mathcal S} p^{\wedge}_{\operatorname{gl}} \ = \ (\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})_\infty \]
  and a lax symmetric monoidal functor
  \[ \gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge \ : \ \operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge}\  \longrightarrow \ {\mathcal S} p^{\wedge}_{\operatorname{gl}} \]
  whose underlying functor
  \[ \gamma_{\operatorname{gl}} = (\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})_{\langle 1\rangle}\ : \ \operatorname{Sp}^O \ \longrightarrow \ ({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^{\wedge})_{\langle 1\rangle} = {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\]
  is a localization of the 1-category of orthogonal spectra at the class of global equivalences.
  We refer to the underlying $\infty$-category ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  as the {\em $\infty$-category of global spectra}, and to the monoidal structure as the
  {\em global smash product}.
<!-- end construction-21 -->
<!-- theorem-20: body_md -->
\label{thm:Sp_gl properties}\
  \begin{enumerate}[\em (i)]
  \item The $\infty$-category ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ of global spectra 
    is stable and compactly generated, and hence presentable.
  \item 
    The symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category ${\mathcal S} p^{\wedge}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ of global spectra
    is presentably symmetric monoidal.
  \item The $\infty$-category $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)$
    of commutative global ring spectra is presentable.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-20 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
(i)
  The $\infty$-category ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is complete and cocomplete
  as the localization of a complete and cocomplete model category,
  see \cite[Theorem 2.5.9]{barnea-harpaz-horel}.
  Since the global model structure of  \cite[Theorem 4.3.18]{schwede:global}
  is stable, the suspension functor on its homotopy category is invertible,
  so the $\infty$-category ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is stable,
  compare \cite[Corollary 1.4.2.27]{lurie:higher_algebra}.
  Moreover, by \cite[Theorem 4.4.3]{schwede:global} the triangulated homotopy category
  of the stable $\infty$-category of global spectra
  is compactly generated by the unreduced suspension spectra of the global classifying spaces
  of all compact Lie groups;  in particular, the $\infty$-category ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  of global spectra is presentable by \cite[Corollary 1.4.4.2]{lurie:higher_algebra}.

  (ii) Because the smash product is a Quillen bifunctor
  for the global model structure, the induced smash product
  on ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves colimits in both variables.
  Since the underlying $\infty$-category is presentable by (i),
  the symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category ${\mathcal S} p^{\wedge}_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  is presentably symmetric monoidal.

  Since ${\mathcal S} p^{\wedge}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is presentably symmetric monoidal by (ii),
  the $\infty$-category $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ of its commutative algebras
  is presentable by \cite[Corollary 3.2.3.5]{lurie:higher_algebra}, proving (iii).
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- construction-22: body_md -->
\label{con:res_G}
  We consider the functor of 1-categories
  \[ (-)_G \ : \ \operatorname{Sp}^O\ \longrightarrow \ \operatorname{Sp}_G^O \ , \quad X \ \longmapsto \ X_G\]
  from orthogonal spectra to orthogonal $G$-spectra
  that endows an orthogonal spectrum with the trivial $G$-action.
  This functor takes global equivalences to ${\underline \pi}_*$-isomorphisms.
  The `equivariant' smash product of orthogonal $G$-spectra is simply the smash
  product of the underlying non-equivariant orthogonal spectra
  with diagonal $G$-action. So the trivial action functor $(-)_G$ is strong symmetric monoidal
  for the respective smash products.
  The universal property of the monoidal localization $\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge$
  thus yields a unique lax symmetric monoidal functor of symmetric monoidal $\infty$-categories
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:define_res^sm_G}
    \operatorname{res}_G^{\wedge} \ : \ {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^{\wedge} \ \longrightarrow \ {\mathcal S} p_G^{\wedge}    
  \end{equation}
  equipped with a homotopy witnessing the commutativity of the following square on the left:
  \[ \xymatrix@C=12mm{
      \operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge}\ar[r]^-{\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}}\ar[d]_{(-)_G^\wedge} &  {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge \ar[d]^{\operatorname{res}_G^\wedge}   &&
      \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})\ar[r]^-{\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})}\ar[d]_{\operatorname{CAlg}((-)_G^\wedge)} &  \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge) \ar[d]^{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{res}_G^\wedge)}      \\
       \operatorname{Sp}_G^{O,\wedge} \ar[r]_-{\gamma_G^\wedge} & {\mathcal S} p_G^\wedge &&
       \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}_G^{O,\wedge}) \ar[r]_-{\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma_G^\wedge)} & \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_G^\wedge)
     } \]
   The underlying  functor
   \[ \operatorname{res}_G \ : \ {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\ \longrightarrow \ {\mathcal S} p_G \]
   of $\operatorname{res}_G^\wedge$ is then descended from the trivial action functor
   by the universal property of the localization $\gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{Sp}^O\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$.
   While a priori only lax, we show in the next theorem that
   $\operatorname{res}_G^{\wedge}$ is in fact strong symmetric monoidal.
   Lax symmetric monoidal functors induce
   functors of commutative algebras, yielding the
   commutative square of $\infty$-categories on the right.
<!-- end construction-22 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:CAlg_left_adjoint}
  Let $F\colon {\mathcal C}\longrightarrow{\mathcal D}$ be a strong symmetric monoidal functor
  between symmetric monoidal $\infty$-categories
  whose underlying functor $F_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon {\mathcal C}_{\langle 1\rangle}\longrightarrow {\mathcal D}_{\langle 1\rangle}$ is a left adjoint.
  Then $F\colon {\mathcal C}\longrightarrow{\mathcal D}$ is a left adjoint relative to $\operatorname{\mathcal{F}in}_*$,
  the functor  $\operatorname{CAlg}(F)\colon \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal C})\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal D})$
  has a right adjoint, and the commutative square
    \[ \xymatrix@C=12mm@R=7mm{
        \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal C})\ar[d]_{\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}} \ar[r]^-{\operatorname{CAlg}(F)} &
        \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal D})\ar[d]^{\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}}\\
        {\mathcal C}_{\langle 1\rangle}\ar[r]_-{F_{\langle 1\rangle}}  & {\mathcal D}_{\langle 1\rangle}
      } \]
    is horizontally right adjointable.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
By \cite[Corollary 7.3.2.7]{lurie:higher_algebra}, the functor $F$
  has a relative right adjoint $G\colon {\mathcal D}\longrightarrow{\mathcal C}$ over $\operatorname{\mathcal{F}in}_*$,
  which is moreover a morphism of operads. So $G$ is a lax symmetric monoidal
  structure on a right adjoint $G_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon {\mathcal D}_{\langle 1\rangle}\longrightarrow{\mathcal C}_{\langle 1\rangle}$ to $F_{\langle 1\rangle}$.
  The unit and counit of the relative adjunction then induce
  the unit and counit of an adjunction between
  $\operatorname{CAlg}(F)\colon \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal C})\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal D})$ and $\operatorname{CAlg}(G)$.
  The horizontal right adjointability of the square is simply the statement
  that the underlying functor of the right adjoint $\operatorname{CAlg}(G)$
  to $\operatorname{CAlg}(F)$ is the right adjoint $G_{\langle 1\rangle}$ to the functor $F_{\langle 1\rangle}$.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- theorem-21: body_md -->
\label{thm:gl2G}
  Let $G$ be a compact Lie group.
  \begin{enumerate}[\em (i)]
    \item The functor
    $\operatorname{res}_G\colon {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_G$ has a left adjoint and a right adjoint.
  \item The functors $\operatorname{res}_G\colon {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p_G$ are jointly conservative
    as $G$ runs over representatives for the isomorphism classes of all compact Lie groups.
  \item The functors $\Phi^G\circ \operatorname{res}_G\colon {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p$ are jointly conservative
    as $G$ runs over representatives for the isomorphism classes of all compact Lie groups.
  \item The  lax symmetric monoidal functor
    $\operatorname{res}_G^{\wedge}\colon {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^{\wedge}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_G^{\wedge}$ is strong symmetric monoidal.
    \item  The functor $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{res}^\wedge_G)$ has a left adjoint and a right adjoint.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-21 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
(i) The functor $\operatorname{res}_G$ is an exact functor between stable $\infty$-categories,
  and the induced functor of triangulated homotopy categories
  $h(\operatorname{res}_G)\colon h({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}})\longrightarrow h({\mathcal S} p_G)$ has adjoints on either side
  by \cite[Theorem 4.5.24]{schwede:global}.
  So $h(\operatorname{res}_G)$ preserves sums and products.
  Hence the functor of $\infty$-categories $\operatorname{res}_G$ is an exact functor
  preserving sums and products, and hence all limits and colimits.
  Since the source and target of $\operatorname{res}_G$  are presentable,
  this functor has adjoints on either side, by Lurie's adjoint functor theorem
  \cite[Corollary 5.5.2.9]{lurie:htt}.
  
  Property (ii) holds by design, since a morphism
  $f\colon X\longrightarrow Y$ of orthogonal spectra is defined to be a global equivalence
  if and only if the morphisms of orthogonal $G$-spectra
  $f_G\colon X_G\longrightarrow Y_G$ are ${\underline \pi}_*$-isomorphisms of orthogonal $G$-spectra
  for all compact Lie groups $G$.
  Property (iii) then follows from property (ii) and
  the fact that the geometric fixed point functors $\Phi^H\circ\operatorname{res}^G_H\colon {\mathcal S} p_G\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p$
  are jointly conservative for all closed subgroups $H$ of $G$,
  see \cite[Proposition 6.13]{mathew-naumann-noel:nilpotence} for an
  $\infty$-categorical treatment, and \cite[Proposition 3.3.10]{schwede:global}
  for a proof in the orthogonal spectrum model.
  We also use implicitly that the functor $\Phi^H\circ\operatorname{res}^G_H\circ \operatorname{res}_G\colon {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p$
  is naturally equivalent to $\Phi^H\circ\operatorname{res}_H$.

  (iv) Strong (versus lax) monoidality can be tested on homotopy categories; 
  at the level of homotopy categories, the argument is explained
  immediately before \cite[Theorem 4.5.24]{schwede:global}.
  The ultimate reason is the fact that for every flat orthogonal spectrum $X$
  (i.e., cofibrant in the global model structure) and every compact Lie group $G$,
  the functor $X_G\wedge-\colon \operatorname{Sp}_G^O\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sp}_G^O$ preserves ${\underline \pi}_*$-isomorphisms,
  see \cite[Theorem 3.5.10]{schwede:global}.
  

  (v) Since $\operatorname{res}_G^\wedge$ is a strong symmetric monoidal left adjoint,
  $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{res}_G^\wedge)$ has a right adjoint by Lemma \ref{lem:CAlg_left_adjoint}.
  For every presentably symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category ${\mathcal C}$,
  the forgetful functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon\allowbreak\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal C})\longrightarrow {\mathcal C}_{\langle 1\rangle}$
  preserves and creates all limits and sifted colimits by
  Corollary 3.2.2.5 and Proposition 3.2.3.1 of  \cite{lurie:higher_algebra}.
  Since $\operatorname{res}_G$ has adjoints on either side, 
  $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{res}_G^\wedge)\sim \operatorname{res}_G\circ\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}$ preserves limits
  and sifted colimits.
  Since  $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}$ is conservative and creates limits and sifted colimits,
  we conclude that the functor $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{res}_G^\wedge)$ preserves limits and sifted colimits.
  Since the source and target of $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{res}_G^\wedge)$ are presentable,
  this functor has a left adjoint
  by the adjoint functor theorem \cite[Corollary 5.5.2.9]{lurie:htt}.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- construction-23: body_md -->
We let $X$ be an orthogonal spectrum, and we let $\gamma\colon K\longrightarrow G$ be a continuous
  epimorphism of compact Lie groups.
  For every $G$-representation $V$, we have $\gamma^*(V)^K=V^G$ and
  \[    X(\gamma^*(V)\oplus{\mathbb R}^m)^K\ = \ \gamma^*(X(V\oplus{\mathbb R}^m))^K
    \ = \ X(V\oplus{\mathbb R}^m)^G\ ,  \]
  because $\gamma$ is surjective.
  We define the {\em inflation homomorphism}
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:define_inflation}
  \gamma^*\ \colon\ \Phi_k^G(X) \ \longrightarrow \ \Phi^K_k(X)   
  \end{equation}
  by sending the class of a based continuous map
  $f\colon S^{V^G\oplus{\mathbb R}^{m+k}}\longrightarrow X(V\oplus{\mathbb R}^m)^G$
  to the class of the same map, but now viewed as a map
  \[ f \ \colon \ S^{\gamma^*(V)^K\oplus {\mathbb R}^{m+k}}\  \longrightarrow \  X(\gamma^*(V)\oplus{\mathbb R}^m)^K\ . \]
  Much like in \cite[Construction 3.1.15]{schwede:global},
  we exploit here that elements of $\Phi_k^K(X)$
  can unambiguously be represented by based maps $S^{W^K\oplus{\mathbb R}^{m+k}}\longrightarrow X(W\oplus{\mathbb R}^m)^K$,
  for any $K$-representation $W$, not necessarily a subrepresentation of the chosen
  complete universe, see \cite[Construction 3.1.13]{schwede:global}.
  The inflation homomorphisms $\gamma^*$ are clearly contravariantly functorial
  for composition of continuous epimorphisms.
  The inflation homomorphism $\gamma^*$
  is a monoidal natural transformation between two lax symmetric monoidal
  functors from orthogonal spectra to graded abelian groups that both invert global equivalences.
  So by monoidal localization, $\gamma^*$ descends uniquely to a
  monoidal natural transformation
  $\gamma^*\colon\bar\Phi_*^G\circ\operatorname{res}^\wedge_G\longrightarrow\bar\Phi^K_*\circ\operatorname{res}^\wedge_K$
  between the descended functors ${\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{GrAb}^\otimes$
  from the $\infty$-category of global spectra to graded abelian groups;
  we abuse notation and denote the descended transformation by the same symbol.
<!-- end construction-23 -->
<!-- construction-24: body_md -->
We let $i_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon {\mathcal S} p^\wedge\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}$ be the unique
  strong symmetric monoidal left adjoint.
  It is fully faithful by \cite[Theorem 4.5.1]{schwede:global},
  and its right adjoint is the forgetful functor
  $\operatorname{res}^\wedge_{\{1\}}\colon {\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p^\wedge$.
  Then the composite
  \[ {\mathcal S} p^\wedge\ \xrightarrow{\ i_{\operatorname{gl}}\ } \ {\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}\ \xrightarrow{\operatorname{res}^\wedge_G}\ {\mathcal S} p^\wedge_G \]
  is a strong symmetric monoidal left adjoint;
  by virtue of ${\mathcal S} p^\wedge$ being initial in $\operatorname{CAlg}(\Pr^L_{\operatorname{st}})$,
  the composite is uniquely monoidally equivalent
  to the inflation functor \eqref{eq:inflation_functor}:
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:i_gl2i_G}
    \operatorname{res}^\wedge_G\circ i_{\operatorname{gl}}\ \sim\  i_G\ . 
  \end{equation}  
  A global spectrum $Y$ is {\em left induced} if it is in the essential
  image of the fully faithful functor $i_{\operatorname{gl}}$.
  In this case, the inflation homomorphism \eqref{eq:define_inflation}
  \[ p_G^* \ \colon \ \bar\pi_k(Y) = \bar\Phi^{\{1\}}_k(Y)\ \longrightarrow\ \bar\Phi_k^G(Y) \]
  associated to the unique homomorphism $p_G\colon G\longrightarrow\{1\}$
  is an isomorphism, see \cite[Example 4.5.10]{schwede:global}.
  In particular, for every non-equivariant spectrum $X$ in ${\mathcal S} p$,
  the inflation homomorphism
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:p_G_iso}
    p_G^* \ \colon \ \bar\pi_*(X)\ \cong_{\eqref{eq:i_gl2i_G}}\
    \bar\Phi^{\{1\}}_*(i_{\operatorname{gl}}(X))\ \longrightarrow\ \bar\Phi_*^G(i_{\operatorname{gl}}(X))
   \ \cong_{\eqref{eq:i_gl2i_G}}\  \bar\Phi^G_*(i_G(X))   
  \end{equation}
  is a monoidal natural isomorphism between lax symmetric monoidal
  functors ${\mathcal S} p^\wedge\longrightarrow\operatorname{GrAb}^\otimes$.
<!-- end construction-24 -->
<!-- prop-13: body_md -->
\label{prop:identify_Phis}
  There is a unique monoidal natural transformation
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:Phi_vs_Phi}
    \tau \ \colon \
    \bar\pi_*\circ \Phi^G \ \longrightarrow\ \bar\Phi^G_*
  \end{equation}
of lax monoidal functors ${\mathcal S} p^\wedge_G\longrightarrow\operatorname{GrAb}^\otimes$  such that the composite
  \[  \bar\pi_* \ \xrightarrow[\cong]{\bar\pi_*\circ \eqref{eq:Phi_p_G}}\
    \bar\pi_*\circ \Phi^G \circ i_G\ \xrightarrow[\cong]{\tau\circ i_G}\
    \bar\Phi^G_*\circ i_G    \]
  equals the monoidal isomorphism $p_G^*$ from \eqref{eq:p_G_iso}.
  Moreover, $\tau$ is a monoidal natural isomorphism.
<!-- end prop-13 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
For every orthogonal $G$-spectrum $X$,
  the geometric fixed point functor $\Phi^G_k\colon\operatorname{Sp}^O_G\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ab}$
  inverts the morphism $X\wedge i\colon X\longrightarrow X\wedge\tilde E{\mathcal P}$, simply because
  the $G$-fixed point functor $(-)^G$ is strong monoidal for the smash product
  of based $G$-spaces, and the map $i^G\colon S^0=(S^0)^G\longrightarrow (\tilde E{\mathcal P})^G$ is a homeomorphism.
  So the descended functor $\bar\Phi^G_k\colon{\mathcal S} p_G\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ab}$
  inverts geometric fixed point equivalences.
  The functor $\bar\pi_*\circ\Phi^G$ also 
  inverts geometric fixed point equivalences, so both $\bar\Phi^G_* $ and $\bar\pi_*\circ\Phi^G$
  are objects of the $\infty$-category $\operatorname{Fun}_{\operatorname{lax}}^{\tilde E{\mathcal P}}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_G,\operatorname{GrAb}^\otimes)$.
  Theorem \ref{thm:Phi_mon_loc} shows that the functor
  \[
    \operatorname{Fun}_{\operatorname{lax}}(i_G,\operatorname{GrAb}^\otimes) \colon  \operatorname{Fun}_{\operatorname{lax}}^{\tilde E{\mathcal P}}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_G,\operatorname{GrAb}^\otimes) \ \longrightarrow \
    \operatorname{Fun}_{\operatorname{lax}}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge,\operatorname{GrAb}^\otimes) \]
  is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories, which proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:fix_ring_iso}
  Let $R$ be a homotopy $G$-ring spectrum.
  The value of the monoidal natural isomorphism \eqref{eq:Phi_vs_Phi}
  at the underlying $G$-spectrum of $R$ is an isomorphism of graded rings
  from $\bar\pi_*(\Phi^G(R))$ to $\bar\Phi^G_*(R)$.
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- construction-25: body_md -->
\label{con:Mod(D)}
We let ${\mathcal D}$ be a symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category.
In \cite[Definition 3.3.3.8]{lurie:higher_algebra}, 
Lurie defines an $\infty$-operad $\operatorname{Mod}^\otimes({\mathcal D})$
that comes with a functor $\pi_{\mathcal D}\colon \operatorname{Mod}^\otimes({\mathcal D})\longrightarrow {\mathcal D}\times \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal D})$;
Lurie uses the notation $\operatorname{Mod}^{\text{Comm}}({\mathcal D})^\otimes$
and works more generally over coherent $\infty$-operads;
we only need the case of the commutative operad.
Objects of $\operatorname{Mod}^\otimes({\mathcal D})$ can informally be thought of as pairs $(M,T)$
consisting of a commutative algebra $T$ in ${\mathcal D}$, and a left $T$-module $M$.
And morphisms are, informally speaking, pairs $(f,i)\colon (M,T)\longrightarrow (M',T')$
consisting of a morphism $i\colon T\longrightarrow T'$ of commutative algebras,
and a morphism of $T$-modules $f\colon M\longrightarrow i^*(M')$.
Proposition 3.3.3.10 of \cite{lurie:higher_algebra} characterizes inert morphisms
in $\operatorname{Mod}^\otimes({\mathcal D})$: firstly, the image in $\operatorname{\mathcal{F}in}_*$ is inert; and
secondly, the classifying functor takes certain lifts to inert morphisms of ${\mathcal D}$.

For a commutative algebra $T$, Lurie then defines the $\infty$-operad $\operatorname{Mod}_T^\otimes({\mathcal D})$
as the fiber of $\pi_{\mathcal D}$ over $T$, i.e., by the pullback
\[ \xymatrix{ \operatorname{Mod}_T^\otimes({\mathcal D})\ar[r]\ar[d]_{u_T} & \operatorname{Mod}^\otimes({\mathcal D})\ar[d]^{\pi_{\mathcal D}}\\
{\mathcal D}\ar[r]_-{(-,T)} & {\mathcal D}\times \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal D}),  } \]
see \cite[Definition 4.5.1.1]{lurie:higher_algebra};
Lurie uses the notation $\operatorname{Mod}_T({\mathcal D})^\otimes$.
The left vertical {\em forgetful functor} $u_T\colon \operatorname{Mod}_T^\otimes({\mathcal D})\longrightarrow{\mathcal D}$ is a morphism
of $\infty$-operads, because $u_T$ preserves and detects inertness in the sense explained above.

Now we let $R\colon {\mathcal D}\longrightarrow{\mathcal C}$ be a lax symmetric monoidal functor.
Postcomposition with $R$ is a functor
$\operatorname{Mod}^\otimes(R)\colon \operatorname{Mod}^\otimes({\mathcal D})\longrightarrow \operatorname{Mod}^\otimes({\mathcal C})$
that participates in a commutative diagram:
\[ \xymatrix@C=25mm{
{\mathcal D}\ar[r]^-{(-,T)}\ar[d]_R &    {\mathcal D}\times \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal D}) \ar[d]^{R\times\operatorname{CAlg}(R)}&
 \operatorname{Mod}^\otimes({\mathcal D})\ar[d]^{\operatorname{Mod}^\otimes(R)}\ar[l]_-{\pi_{\mathcal D}}\\
{\mathcal C} \ar[r]_-{(-,\operatorname{CAlg}(R)(T))}&  {\mathcal C}\times \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal C})   & \operatorname{Mod}^\otimes({\mathcal C})\ar[l]^-{\pi_{\mathcal C}}} \]
Passing to pullbacks yields a functor
\[ \operatorname{Mod}(T|R)\ \colon \ \operatorname{Mod}_T^\otimes({\mathcal D}) \ \longrightarrow \ \operatorname{Mod}_{\operatorname{CAlg}(R)(T)}^\otimes({\mathcal C}) \]
that covers $R$ with respect to the forgetful functors.
Because $R$ preserves inert morphisms,
postcomposition with $R$ preserves the second condition that characterizes
inert morphisms in $\operatorname{Mod}^\otimes({\mathcal D})$.
So $\operatorname{Mod}^\otimes(R)$, and hence $\operatorname{Mod}(T|R)$, preserve inert morphisms,
and $\operatorname{Mod}(T|R)$ is a morphism of $\infty$-operads.

In \cite[Theorem 4.5.2.1]{lurie:higher_algebra}, Lurie shows that
if the underlying $\infty$-category ${\mathcal D}_{\langle 1\rangle}$
admits geometric realization of simplicial objects,
and if the tensor product functor $\otimes\colon{\mathcal D}_{\langle 1\rangle}\times{\mathcal D}_{\langle 1\rangle}\longrightarrow{\mathcal D}_{\langle 1\rangle}$
preserves such geometric realizations in each variable separately,
then $\operatorname{Mod}_T^\otimes({\mathcal D})$ is in fact a symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category.
As a morphism of $\infty$-operads between symmetric monoidal $\infty$-categories,
the forgetful functor $u_T\colon \operatorname{Mod}_T^\otimes({\mathcal D})\longrightarrow{\mathcal D}$ is then
lax symmetric monoidal.
Moreover $u_T$ is the right adjoint in a relative adjunction over $\operatorname{\mathcal{F}in}_*$.
The left adjoint $T\otimes-\colon{\mathcal D}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}_T^\otimes({\mathcal D})$,
the {\em free $T$-module functor}, is moreover strong symmetric monoidal.
To obtain this monoidal adjunction, we can appeal to \cite[Theorem 4.5.3.1]{lurie:higher_algebra}
for the unique morphism ${\mathbbm 1}\longrightarrow T$ in $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal D})$
from an initial commutative algebra,
and then exploit \cite[Proposition 3.4.2.1]{lurie:higher_algebra}
to identify $\operatorname{Mod}_{{\mathbbm 1}}^\otimes({\mathcal D})$ with ${\mathcal D}$.

If ${\mathcal C}$ and ${\mathcal D}$ are symmetric monoidal $\infty$-categories that both
satisfy the hypotheses of \cite[Theorem 4.5.2.1]{lurie:higher_algebra},
then for every lax symmetric monoidal functor $R\colon {\mathcal D}\longrightarrow{\mathcal C}$, the functor
$\operatorname{Mod}(T|R)\colon\operatorname{Mod}_T^\otimes({\mathcal D})\allowbreak\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}_{\operatorname{CAlg}(R)(T)}^\otimes({\mathcal C})$
is a morphism of $\infty$-operads between symmetric monoidal $\infty$-categories,
i.e., again a lax symmetric monoidal functor.
<!-- end construction-25 -->
<!-- theorem-22: body_md -->
\label{thm:monoidal_loc}
  For every commutative orthogonal ring spectrum $A$,
  the lax symmetric monoidal functor
  \[  \operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})  \ \colon\     \operatorname{Mod}_A^\wedge\ \longrightarrow\
      \operatorname{Mod}^\otimes_{\gamma(A)}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\]
    is a monoidal localization.
<!-- end theorem-22 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
We let
  \[ \gamma^\wedge_A\ : \ \operatorname{Mod}^\wedge_A \ \longrightarrow \ {\mathcal M} od^\wedge_A \]
  be a monoidal localization of the global model structure.
  We write ${\mathcal M} od_A=({\mathcal M} od^\wedge_A)_{\langle 1\rangle}$ for the underlying $\infty$-category.
  The following diagram of lax symmetric monoidal functors commutes:
   \[ \xymatrix@C=20mm{ \operatorname{Mod}^\wedge_A =\operatorname{Mod}^\otimes_A(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})
       \ar[r]^-{\operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})}\ar[d]_{u_A} &
      \operatorname{Mod}_{\gamma(A)}^\otimes({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\ar[d]^{u_{\gamma(A)}}\\
      \operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge}\ar[r]_-{\gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge} & {\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}
    } \]
  The composite $\gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge\circ u_A$ inverts global equivalences,
  and the functor $u_{\gamma(A)}$ is conservative.
  So the functor $\operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\colon\operatorname{Mod}_A^\wedge \longrightarrow
  \operatorname{Mod}_{\gamma(A)}^\otimes({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ inverts global equivalences.
  The universal property of the monoidal localization provides a unique
  lax symmetric monoidal functor
  \[\sigma\ \colon\ {\mathcal M} od_A^\wedge\ \longrightarrow\ \operatorname{Mod}^\otimes_{\gamma(A)}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)  \]
  equipped with a monoidal equivalence
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:descend Mod(A)}
    \sigma\circ \gamma^\wedge_A \ \sim \ \operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\ .
  \end{equation}
  We define a lax symmetric monoidal functor by
  \[ \rho\ = \ u_{\gamma(A)}\circ \sigma\ \colon \ {\mathcal M} od^\wedge_A\ \longrightarrow \ {\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}\ . \]
  The monoidal equivalence 
  \[    \rho\circ \gamma^\wedge_A \ =\
      u_{\gamma(A)}\circ\sigma\circ \gamma^\wedge_A \ \sim_{\eqref{eq:descend Mod(A)}} \
    u_{\gamma(A)}\circ \operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\ =\ \gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge\circ u_A \]
  witnesses the commutativity of the following square:
  \begin{equation}\begin{aligned}\label{eq:forget and F}
      \xymatrix@C=12mm{
      \operatorname{Mod}^\wedge_A \ar[d]_{\gamma^\wedge_A}\ar[r]^-{u_A}
      & \operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge}\ar[d]^{\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}}  \\
      {\mathcal M} od_A^\wedge\ar[r]_-{\rho} & {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge }
    \end{aligned}
  \end{equation}
  So the lax symmetric monoidal functor $\rho$ `is' the monoidal descendant
  of the forgetful functor $u_A$.
    
  The forgetful functor $u_A\colon\operatorname{Mod}_A\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sp}^O$
  is a right Quillen functor for the global model structures.
  Since the underlying functor $\rho_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon {\mathcal M} od_A\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ of $\rho$
  is descended from a right Quillen functor,
  it is a right adjoint, see \cite[Theorem 2.1]{mazelgee:adjunctions}.
  In particular, $\rho_{\langle 1\rangle}$ preserves limits.
  Also, because the functor $u_A$ detects and preserves global equivalences,
  its derived functor $\rho_{\langle 1\rangle}$ is conservative.
 
  Now we show that $\rho_{\langle 1\rangle}$ also preserves colimits.
  The global model structure on $\operatorname{Mod}_A$ is stable, hence so is
  the associated $\infty$-category ${\mathcal M} od_A$.
  Since the $\infty$-category ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is also stable,
  and since $\rho_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon {\mathcal M} od_A\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves limits,
  it therefore also preserves finite colimits.
  Arbitrary coproducts (i.e., wedges) of orthogonal spectra, and hence also of $A$-modules,
  are homotopical for global equivalences by \cite[Corollary 3.1.37 (i)]{schwede:global}.
  So coproducts in $\operatorname{Sp}^O$ and in $\operatorname{Mod}_A$ represent coproducts
  in ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ and ${\mathcal M} od_A$, respectively. Since the functor $u_A\colon\operatorname{Mod}_A\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sp}^O$
  preserves arbitrary coproducts, so does the descended functor $\rho_{\langle 1\rangle}$.
  Since $\rho_{\langle 1\rangle}$ preserves finite colimits and arbitrary coproducts,
  it preserves arbitrary colimits.
  
  Lurie shows in \cite{lurie:higher_algebra} that
  the forgetful functor $u_{\gamma(A)}\colon \operatorname{Mod}_{\gamma(A)}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  is conservative and preserves limits and colimits,
  see his Corollary 4.2.3.2 for conservativity, 
  Corollary 4.2.3.3 for limits, and Corollary 4.2.3.5 for colimits,
  using the identification of $\operatorname{Mod}_{\gamma(A)}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$
  with left modules $\operatorname{LMod}_{\gamma(A)}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ from Corollary 4.5.1.6.
  Since $\rho_{\langle 1\rangle}=u_{\gamma(A)}\circ\sigma_{\langle 1\rangle}$
  is conservative and preserves limits and colimits,
  we conclude that also the functor $\sigma_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon{\mathcal M} od_A\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}_{\gamma(A)}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$
  that underlies $\sigma$ is conservative and preserves limits and colimits.

  By \cite[Theorem 4.3.27 (ii)]{schwede:global},
  the functor $A\wedge-\colon\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge}\longrightarrow \operatorname{Mod}^\wedge_A$ preserves global equivalences
  between cofibrant orthogonal spectra, and it sends cofibrant orthogonal spectra
  to cofibrant $A$-modules. So the restricted functor
  \[ (A\wedge-)|_{\operatorname{cof}}\ \colon \ \operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge}_{\operatorname{cof}}\ \longrightarrow\ \operatorname{Mod}^\wedge_{A,\operatorname{cof}} \]
  is strong symmetric monoidal and preserves global equivalences.
  The strong symmetric monoidal composite
  \[    \operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge}_{\operatorname{cof}}\ \xrightarrow{(A\wedge-)|_{\operatorname{cof}}}\ \operatorname{Mod}^\wedge_{A,\operatorname{cof}} \
    \xrightarrow{\gamma^\wedge_{A,\operatorname{cof}}}\ {\mathcal M} od^\wedge_A\]
  thus inverts global equivalences. The modified universal property
  of Remark \ref{rk:monloc_addendum} (iii) provides a unique
  strong symmetric monoidal functor
  \[ L\ \colon\ {\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}\ \longrightarrow\ {\mathcal M} od^\wedge_A \]
  equipped with a monoidal equivalence
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:descend L}
    L\circ \gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl},\operatorname{cof}} \ \sim \ \gamma_A^\wedge\circ (A\wedge -)|_{\operatorname{cof}}\ .
  \end{equation}

  By \cite[Theorem 2.1]{mazelgee:adjunctions} applied to the Quillen pair $(A\wedge-,u_A)$,
  their derived functors are adjoint.
  The derived functor of $A\wedge-$ is $L_{\langle 1\rangle}$ by \eqref{eq:descend L},
  and that of $u_A$ is $\rho_{\langle 1\rangle}$ by \eqref{eq:forget and F},
  so $(L_{\langle 1\rangle},\rho_{\langle 1\rangle})$ is an adjoint functor pair.
  We claim that the $\infty$-category ${\mathcal M} od_A$ is generated under colimits by
  the image of the descended left adjoint $L_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow {\mathcal M} od_A$.  
  As the localization of a model category, the $\infty$-category
  ${\mathcal M} od_A$ is cocomplete, see \cite[Theorem 2.5.9]{barnea-harpaz-horel}.
  We showed above that the right adjoint $\rho_{\langle 1\rangle}$ is conservative and
  preserves colimits. So $\rho_{\langle 1\rangle}$ is monadic by Lurie's
  Barr--Beck theorem \cite[Theorem 4.7.3.5]{lurie:higher_algebra}.
  Hence every object of ${\mathcal M} od_A$ can be presented as a colimit of a diagram
  all of whose values are in the essential image of $L_{\langle 1\rangle}$, see 
  \cite[Proposition 4.7.3.14]{lurie:higher_algebra}.
  In particular,  the $\infty$-category ${\mathcal M} od_A$ is generated under colimits by
  the objects in the image of $L_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow {\mathcal M} od_A$.

  Now we will show that $\sigma$ is strong, and not only lax, symmetric monoidal.
  The {\em monoidal mate} of the commutative diagram of lax symmetric monoidal functors
  \[ \xymatrix{
      \operatorname{Mod}^\wedge_A\ar[r]^-{u_A}\ar[d]_{\operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})}&    \operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge}\ar[d]^{\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}}  \\
      \operatorname{Mod}^\otimes_{\gamma(A)}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\ar[r]_-{u_{\gamma(A)}} &{\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}   } \]
  is the composite monoidal transformation
  \begin{align}\label{eq:some_mon_tran}
    (\gamma(A)\wedge -)\circ \gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}\ &\xrightarrow{  (\gamma(A)\wedge -)\circ \gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}\circ\text{unit}}
    \
    (\gamma(A)\wedge -)\circ \gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}\circ u_A \circ(A\wedge -) \\
      &=\  (\gamma(A)\wedge -)\circ u_{\gamma(A)} \circ \operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\circ(A\wedge -) \nonumber\\
&\xrightarrow{\text{counit}\circ\operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\circ (A\wedge -)} \  \operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\circ (A\wedge -)  \ . \nonumber
  \end{align}
  The underlying morphism in ${\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}$ of the value of  \eqref{eq:some_mon_tran} at
  an orthogonal spectrum $X$ is the monoidal structure morphism
  \[  \gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}(A)\wedge \gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}(X)\ \longrightarrow \ \gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}(A\wedge X)\]
  of $\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}$.
  This monoidal structure morphism is an equivalence on pairs of cofibrant objects,
  by Remark \ref{rk:monloc_addendum} (ii).
  Moreover, for cofibrant orthogonal spectra $X$, the functor $-\wedge X$ is fully homotopical
  for global equivalences by \cite[Theorem 4.3.27 (i)]{schwede:global}.
  So by cofibrant replacement, the monoidal structure morphism is an equivalence
  already if only $X$ is cofibrant.
  So when restricted to cofibrant orthogonal spectra,
  the monoidal transformation \eqref{eq:some_mon_tran}
  is a monoidal equivalence, witnessing that the restricted mate diagram 
  \[ \xymatrix@C=15mm{
      \operatorname{Mod}^\wedge_{A,\operatorname{cof}}\ar[d]_{\operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})_{\operatorname{cof}}}
      &    \operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge}_{\operatorname{cof}}\ar[d]^{\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl},\operatorname{cof}}}\ar[l]_-{(A\wedge-)|_{\operatorname{cof}}}  \\
      \operatorname{Mod}^\otimes_{\gamma(A)}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}) &{\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}} \ar[l]^-{\gamma(A)\wedge-}  } \]
  commutes.
  Here $\operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})_{\operatorname{cof}}$ denotes the restriction
  of $\operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ to cofibrant $A$-modules.
  Since the functors $\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl},\operatorname{cof}}$
  and $\gamma(A)\wedge-$ are strong symmetric monoidal,
  so is their composite,
  and thus also the functor $\operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)_{\operatorname{cof}}\circ(A\wedge-)|_{\operatorname{cof}}$.
  The monoidal equivalences
  \[ \sigma\circ L\circ \gamma_{\operatorname{gl},\operatorname{cof}}^\wedge\ \sim \
    \sigma\circ \gamma_{A,\operatorname{cof}}^\wedge\circ(A\wedge-)|_{\operatorname{cof}}\ \sim \
    \operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)_{\operatorname{cof}}\circ(A\wedge-)|_{\operatorname{cof}}\]
  then show that the lax symmetric monoidal functor
  $ \sigma\circ L\circ \gamma_{\operatorname{gl},\operatorname{cof}}^\wedge\colon\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge}_{\operatorname{cof}}\longrightarrow \operatorname{Mod}^\otimes_{\gamma(A)}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is strong.
  The first monoidal equivalence is \eqref{eq:descend L} composed with $\sigma$;
  the second is \eqref{eq:descend Mod(A)}, restricted to cofibrant $A$-modules,
  and composed with $(A\wedge-)|_{\operatorname{cof}}$.

  The restricted monoidal localization functor
  $\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl},\operatorname{cof}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}_{\operatorname{cof}}^{O,\wedge}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  is strong and essentially surjective on objects, so it detects strongness
  as explained in Remark \ref{rk:monloc_addendum} (ii).
  Hence the lax symmetric monoidal functor
  $\sigma\circ L\colon{\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow \operatorname{Mod}^\otimes_{\gamma(A)}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is strong.
  The monoidal products of both ${\mathcal M} od^\wedge_A$ and $\operatorname{Mod}^\otimes_{\gamma(A)}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$
  preserve colimits in each variable.
  Indeed, in ${\mathcal M} od^\wedge_A$ we may consider an object of the form $\gamma_A(M)$
  for a cofibrant $A$-module $M$. Then $\gamma_A(M)\otimes-$
  is a total left derived functor of the left Quillen functor $M\wedge_A-$,
  and hence a left adjoint. And for $\operatorname{Mod}^\otimes_{\gamma(A)}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$,
  this is \cite[Theorem 3.4.4.2]{lurie:higher_algebra} for ${\mathcal O}={\mathcal C} omm$,
  saying that $\operatorname{Mod}^\otimes_{\gamma(A)}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is presentably symmetric monoidal.
  Since $\sigma_{\langle 1\rangle}$ preserves colimits, and since the $\infty$-category ${\mathcal M} od_A$
  is generated under colimits by the image of the strong 
  symmetric monoidal left adjoint $L\colon {\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal M} od^\wedge_A$,
  we conclude that $\sigma\colon {\mathcal M} od^\wedge_A\longrightarrow \operatorname{Mod}^\otimes_{\gamma(A)}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$
  is strong, as claimed.
  
  Now we show that $\sigma$ is an equivalence of underlying $\infty$-categories.
  To this end we apply \cite[Corollary 4.7.3.16]{lurie:higher_algebra},
  including its addendum, 
  to the functors $\sigma_{\langle 1\rangle}$, $u_{\gamma(A)}$
  and $\rho_{\langle 1\rangle}=u_{\gamma(A)}\circ\sigma_{\langle 1\rangle}$.
  We need to verify the hypotheses of Lurie's result.
  We argued above that $(L_{\langle 1\rangle},\rho_{\langle 1\rangle})$ is an adjoint functor pair.
  Also, $(\gamma(A)\wedge-,u_{\gamma(A)})$ is an adjoint functor pair,
  so hypothesis (1) holds.
  The $\infty$-categories ${\mathcal M} od_A$ and $\operatorname{Mod}_{\gamma(A)}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$
  admit all colimits, and both $\rho_{\langle 1\rangle}$ and $u_{\gamma(A)}$
  are conservative and preserve all colimits, verifying hypotheses (2), (3), (4)
  and the hypothesis of the addendum. The hypothesis that is most involved to
  verify is (5); in its equivalent form of 
  \cite[Remark 4.7.3.17]{lurie:higher_algebra}, it asks that the following
  composite natural transformation of endofunctors of ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is an equivalence:
  \begin{align*}
    u_{\gamma(A)}\circ (\gamma(A)\wedge -)
    \xrightarrow{u_{\gamma(A)}\circ(\gamma(A)\wedge-)\circ\text{unit}}
    \ &u_{\gamma(A)}\circ (\gamma(A)\wedge- )\circ \rho_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ L_{\langle 1\rangle}\\
    =
    \quad &u_{\gamma(A)}\circ (\gamma(A)\wedge- )\circ u_{\gamma(A)}\circ\sigma_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ L_{\langle 1\rangle}\\
    \xrightarrow{u_{\gamma(A)}\circ \text{counit}\circ\sigma_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ L_{\langle 1\rangle}}\
      &u_{\gamma(A)}\circ \sigma_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ L_{\langle 1\rangle} =
        \rho_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ L_{\langle 1\rangle}\ . 
  \end{align*}
  It suffices to show that this transformation
  becomes an equivalence after precomposition with
  the essentially surjective functor $\gamma_{\operatorname{gl},\operatorname{cof}}\colon\operatorname{Sp}^O_{\operatorname{cof}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$.
  Under the identifications \eqref{eq:forget and F} and \eqref{eq:descend L},
  the unit of the derived adjunction $(L_{\langle 1\rangle},\rho_{\langle 1\rangle})$
  corresponds to the image under $\gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  of the 1-categorical adjunction unit $X\longrightarrow u_A(A\wedge X)$,
  see the proof of \cite[Theorem 2.1]{mazelgee:adjunctions}.
  So the composite with $\gamma_{\operatorname{gl},\operatorname{cof}}$
  is homotopic to the following composite of equivalences:
  \begin{align*}
    u_{\gamma(A)}\circ (\gamma(A)\wedge -)\circ\gamma_{\operatorname{gl},\operatorname{cof}}  \
    _{\eqref{eq:some_mon_tran}}&\sim \
                                 u_{\gamma(A)}\circ \operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ(A\wedge -)|_{\operatorname{cof}}  \\
                               &= \ \gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}\circ u_A\circ(A\wedge -)|_{\operatorname{cof}}  \\
    _{\eqref{eq:forget and F}} &\sim \ \rho_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ\gamma_A\circ(A\wedge -)|_{\operatorname{cof}}  \\
    _{\eqref{eq:descend L}}&\sim \ \rho_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ L_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ\gamma_{\operatorname{gl},\operatorname{cof}} \
  \end{align*}
  This completes the verification of the hypothesis of 
  \cite[Corollary 4.7.3.16]{lurie:higher_algebra},
  which then shows that the functor $\sigma_{\langle 1\rangle}$ is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories.

We have now shown that $\sigma\colon{\mathcal M} od_A^\wedge\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}^\otimes_{\gamma(A)}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)$
is an equivalence of symmetric monoidal $\infty$-categories.
So the functor $\operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ coincides with the monoidal localization
$\gamma^\wedge_A$ up to composition with an equivalence, by \eqref{eq:descend Mod(A)}.
So $\operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is itself a monoidal localization.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- defn-9: body_md -->
\label{def:com_global_ring}
  The {\em $\infty$-category of ultra-commutative ring spectra}  $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  is the localization of the 1-category of commutative orthogonal ring spectra
  at the class of morphisms that are global equivalences of underlying orthogonal spectra.
  We denote the localization functor by
  \[ \gamma^{\operatorname{uc}}_{\operatorname{gl}}\ : \  \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})\  \longrightarrow \ \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}} \ .\]
<!-- end defn-9 -->
<!-- construction-26: body_md -->
We define another `forgetful' functor
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:ucom2CR_gl}
    u_{\operatorname{gl}}\ :\ \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\ \longrightarrow\  \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge) 
  \end{equation}
  from ultra-commutative ring spectra to commutative global ring spectra.
  The monoidal localization $\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}:\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge}\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge$ induces a functor
  \[  \operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge) \ :\  \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})\ \ \longrightarrow \ \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}) \]
  from the 1-category of commutative orthogonal ring spectra to the
  $\infty$-category of commutative global ring spectra.
  Since the functor $\gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}=(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})_{\langle 1\rangle}$ inverts global equivalences
  and the functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is conservative,
  the functor  $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)$ sends global equivalences
  of commutative orthogonal ring spectra to equivalences in $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$.
  So the universal property of localizations
  provides an essentially unique functor \eqref{eq:ucom2CR_gl}
  equipped with a natural equivalence
  \[  u_{\operatorname{gl}} \circ\gamma^{\operatorname{uc}}_{\operatorname{gl}}\ \sim\ \operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\ .     \]
<!-- end construction-26 -->
<!-- theorem-23: body_md -->
\label{thm:UR_monadic}\ 
  \begin{enumerate}[\em (i)]
  \item 
    The functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is monadic
    and preserves sifted colimits. 
  \item  The $\infty$-category $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ of ultra-commutative ring spectra
    is presentable.
  \item
    The functor $u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)$ is both monadic and comonadic.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-23 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
As the localization of a model structure established in \cite[Theorem 5.4.3]{schwede:global},
  the $\infty$-category $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is complete and cocomplete
  by \cite[Theorem 2.5.9]{barnea-harpaz-horel}.
  We shall show that the functor
  \[ \operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\colon \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}) \]
  preserves two particular kinds of colimits:
  \begin{enumerate}[(1)]
  \item The functor $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ takes pushouts along cofibrations
    between cofibrant commutative orthogonal ring spectra to pushouts in $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$.
  \item The functor $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$
    takes coproducts of cofibrant commutative orthogonal ring spectra to coproducts.
  \end{enumerate}
  Granted this for the moment, we now deduce from (1) and (2) the fact that
  \begin{enumerate}[(1)]\setcounter{enumi}{2}
  \item the functor $u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ preserves all colimits.
  \end{enumerate}  
  To prove (3), we exploit that the cofibrations and weak equivalences
  of the global model category structure from \cite[Theorem 5.4.3]{schwede:global}
  make the category $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$ of commutative orthogonal ring spectra
  into a {\em category with weak equivalences and cofibrations}
  in the sense of Cisinski \cite[Definition 7.4.12]{cisinski:book}
  that is moreover {\em homotopy cocomplete}
  in the sense of \cite[Definition 7.7.2]{cisinski:book}.
  In this language, property (1)
  and the fact that $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ preserves initial objects
  (a special case of (2))
  mean that the functor $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is {\em right exact}
  in the sense of \cite[Definition 7.5.2]{cisinski:book}, with respect
  to the degenerate cofibration structure on the $\infty$-category
  $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$, i.e., where all morphisms are cofibrations,
  and the weak equivalences are the equivalences.
  And property (2) means that the functor $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is {\em homotopy cocontinuous}
  in the sense of \cite[Definition 7.7.2]{cisinski:book}.
  Since the weak equivalences in the degenerate cofibration structure on $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$
  are already invertible, $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is its own localization,
  and the left derived functor of $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is nothing but
  the factorization  $u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$
  through the localization of the source. 
  The dual (opposite) of \cite[Corollary 7.7.5]{cisinski:book} thus shows that $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves
  all colimits.


  Now we show properties (1) and (2). 
  For (1) we consider a commutative algebra $T$ in a symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category ${\mathcal D}$.
  As discussed in Construction \ref{con:Mod(D)},
  the symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category $\operatorname{Mod}_T^\otimes({\mathcal D})$
  comes with a lax symmetric monoidal forgetful functor
  \[ u_T\ \colon \ \operatorname{Mod}^\otimes_T({\mathcal D})\ \longrightarrow \ {\mathcal D}\ .  \]
  The induced functor of commutative algebras
  \[ \operatorname{CAlg}(u_T)\ \colon \ \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Mod}_T^\otimes({\mathcal D}))\ \longrightarrow \ \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal D})  \]
  takes the initial object of the source to $T$; so it lifts to a functor
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:compare_slices}
    \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Mod}_T^\otimes({\mathcal D}))\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim \ } \ T\backslash\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal D})\ ,  
  \end{equation}
  and this lift is an equivalence by \cite[Corollary 3.4.1.7]{lurie:higher_algebra}
  for $\mathcal O=\text{Comm}$.

  Next we consider a commutative orthogonal ring spectrum $A$.
  As before, we denote the commutative global ring spectrum it represents
  by $\gamma(A)=\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})(A)$.
  By Theorem \ref{thm:monoidal_loc}, the lax symmetric monoidal functor
  $\operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is a monoidal localization.
  So the composite
  \[ \operatorname{Mod}_{\operatorname{cof}}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\ \colon\
    \operatorname{Mod}_{A,\operatorname{cof}}^\wedge \xrightarrow{\text{incl}} \operatorname{Mod}_A^\wedge \xrightarrow{\operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})}
    \operatorname{Mod}_{\gamma(A)}^\otimes({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\]
  is strong symmetric monoidal,  see Remark \ref{rk:monloc_addendum} (ii).
  Since finite coproducts in $\infty$-categories of commutative
  algebras are given by the underlying monoidal product, the induced functor
  on $\infty$-categories of commutative algebras preserves finite coproducts.
  This functor features in the composite:
  \begin{equation} \label{eq:THEcomposite}
        \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Mod}_{A,\operatorname{cof}}^\wedge) \ \xrightarrow{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Mod}_{\operatorname{cof}}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}))} \
    \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Mod}_{\gamma(A)}^\otimes({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}))\ \xrightarrow[\sim]{\eqref{eq:compare_slices}}
    \gamma(A)\backslash\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\ .
      \end{equation}
  The first functor in this composite preserves finite coproducts,
  and the second is an equivalence as a special case of \eqref{eq:compare_slices}.
  So also the composite \eqref{eq:THEcomposite} preserves finite coproducts.
  
  Now we can wrap up and prove (1).
  We consider a pushout square in $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$
  \begin{equation}
    \begin{aligned}\label{eq:1-po}
      \xymatrix{A\ar[r]^-j\ar[d]_-i & C\ar[d]^k\\ B\ar[r]_-h & D}   
    \end{aligned}
  \end{equation}
  in which all four commutative orthogonal ring spectra are cofibrant,
  and the morphism $i$ is a cofibration,
  in the global model structure of $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$
  established in \cite[Theorem 5.4.3]{schwede:global}.
  By factoring $j$ as a composite of a cofibration followed by
  a weak equivalence in the global model structure of $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$
  and appealing to the cube lemma we can assume without loss of generality
  that also the morphism $j$ is a cofibration.
  
  We write $l=h i=k j\colon A\longrightarrow D$ for the composite.
  By \cite[Theorem 5.4.3 (ii a)]{schwede:global}, the underlying
  morphisms of $A$-modules of $i$, $j$ and $l$ are cofibrations
  in the global model structure on $A$-modules from 
  \cite[Corollary 4.3.29 (i)]{schwede:global}.
  Since $A$ is cofibrant as a module over itself,
  we conclude that all of $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ have cofibrant underlying $A$-modules.
  So we can---and will---view the pushout square \eqref{eq:1-po}
  as a pushout square in $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Mod}_{A,\operatorname{cof}}^\wedge)$.
  Since $A$ is initial in $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Mod}_{A,\operatorname{cof}}^\wedge)$,
  this means that the morphisms $h\colon B\longrightarrow D$
  and $k\colon C\longrightarrow D$ witness $l\colon A\longrightarrow D$
  as the coproduct of $i\colon A\longrightarrow B$ and
  $j\colon A\longrightarrow C$ in the $\infty$-category $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Mod}_{A,\operatorname{cof}}^\wedge)$.
  Since the composite \eqref{eq:THEcomposite} preserves binary coproducts,
  we conclude that $\gamma(h)$ and $\gamma(k)$ express $\gamma(l)\colon \gamma(A)\longrightarrow\gamma(D)$
  as the coproduct of $\gamma(i)\colon \gamma(A)\longrightarrow\gamma(B)$ and
  $\gamma(j)\colon \gamma(A)\longrightarrow\gamma(C)$
  in the slice $\infty$-category $\gamma(A)\backslash\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$.
  This precisely means that $\gamma$ takes the pushout square \eqref{eq:1-po} to a pushout
  in the $\infty$-category $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$, and we have shown claim (1). 
  
  Now we prove claim (2) by exploiting that infinite coproducts
  are specific filtered colimits of finite coproducts.
  The initial object in both $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$ and $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is given by
  the monoidal unit, the sphere spectrum, with its unique commutative algebra structure.
  So the functor $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ preserves initial objects.
  Since $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ preserves initial objects and
  pushouts along cofibrations between cofibrant objects,
  it also preserves all finite coproducts of cofibrant objects.
  
  Now we let $\{R_i\}_{i\in I}$ be an $I$-indexed family
  of cofibrant objects in the global model structure of $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$.
  We write $P$ for the filtered poset, under inclusion, of finite subsets of $I$.
  We define a functor $\Phi\colon P\longrightarrow \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$ by sending a finite subset $S$ of $I$
  to the coproduct $\bigwedge_{i\in S} R_i$, and an inclusion $S\subset T$
  to the canonical morphism $\bigwedge_S R_i \longrightarrow \bigwedge_T R_i$.
  
  We claim that the underlying $\operatorname{Sp}^O$-valued functor of $\Phi$, i.e., the composite
  \[ P \ \xrightarrow{\ \Phi\ } \ \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge}) \ \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}} \ \operatorname{Sp}^O  \]
  is Reedy cofibrant, i.e., for every finite subset $S$ of $I$, the latching morphism
  \[ l_S\ : \ \operatorname{colim}_{C\subsetneq S}  \Phi(C)_{\langle 1\rangle}\ \longrightarrow \ \Phi(S)_{\langle 1\rangle} \]
  is a flat cofibration of orthogonal spectra; here the colimit in the source of $l_S$ is
  formed over the poset of proper subsets of $S$.
  We prove this by induction over the cardinality of $S$. For $S=\emptyset$
  there are no proper subsets, so the latching morphism is the unique morphism from
  the initial orthogonal spectrum to $\Phi(\emptyset)_{\langle 1\rangle}={\mathbb S}$, and thus a flat cofibration.
  If $S$ is not empty, we choose an $i\in S$ and we set $S'=S\setminus\{i\}$.
  Because the monoidal product preserves colimits in each variable, 
  the latching object can be presented as the following pushout:
  \[ \xymatrix{{\mathbb S}\wedge (\operatorname{colim}_{C\subsetneq S'} \Phi(C)_{\langle 1\rangle})\ar[r]^-{{\mathbb S}\wedge l_{S'}}\ar[d]_{\text{unit}\wedge \operatorname{Id}} &
      {\mathbb S}\wedge \Phi(S')_{\langle 1\rangle}\ar[d]\\
      R_i\wedge (\operatorname{colim}_{C\subsetneq S'} \Phi(C)_{\langle 1\rangle})\ar[r]  & 
      \operatorname{colim}_{C\subsetneq S} \Phi(C)_{\langle 1\rangle}   } \]
  Under this interpretation, the latching morphism
  $l_S\colon\operatorname{colim}_{C\subsetneq S} \Phi(C)_{\langle 1\rangle}\longrightarrow \Phi(S)_{\langle 1\rangle}=R_i\wedge \Phi(S')_{\langle 1\rangle}$ becomes
  the pushout product of the unit morphism ${\mathbb S}\longrightarrow R_i$
  and the latching morphism $l_{S'}\colon\allowbreak\operatorname{colim}_{C\subsetneq S'} \Phi(C)_{\langle 1\rangle}\longrightarrow\Phi(S')_{\langle 1\rangle}$.
  The former is a flat cofibration by \cite[Theorem 5.4.3 (ii c)]{schwede:global},
  and $l_{S'}$ is a flat cofibration by induction.
  So the pushout product property lets us conclude that $l_S$ is a flat cofibration.
  This concludes the proof that the underlying $\operatorname{Sp}^O$-valued functor of $\Phi$ is Reedy cofibrant.

  Now we let $\bar\Phi\colon P^\triangleright\longrightarrow \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$
  be a colimit of $\Phi$. Then the value of $\bar\Phi$ at the cone point
  is in particular a coproduct in the 1-category $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$
  of the family  $\{R_i\}_{i\in I}$.
  We contemplate the following commutative diagram of $\infty$-categories:
  \[ \xymatrix@C=10mm{ P^\triangleright \ar[r]^-{\bar\Phi}\ar@/_1pc/[dr]_-{\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\circ\bar\Phi} &
      \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})\ar[r]^-{\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}} \ar[d]^{\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})} &
      \operatorname{Sp}^O\ar[d]^{\gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}}\\
      &  \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^{\wedge}_{\operatorname{gl}})\ar[r]_-{\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}} &{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}
    } \]
  The 1-categorical forgetful functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})\longrightarrow \operatorname{Sp}^O$
  preserves filtered colimits, so the composite $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ\bar\Phi$
  is a colimit in the 1-category of orthogonal spectra.
  As a colimit of a Reedy cofibrant diagram, it represents
  the colimit in the associated $\infty$-category, i.e., the composite 
  $\gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}\circ \operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ\bar\Phi$ is a colimit in the $\infty$-category ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  of global spectra.
  The functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon  \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  creates filtered colimits by \cite[Proposition 3.2.3.1]{lurie:higher_algebra}.
  So $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\circ \bar\Phi$ is a colimit in $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$.
  We have already shown that $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ preserves finite coproducts,
  so for every finite subset $S$ of $I$, the object $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})(\Phi(S))$
  is a coproduct  in $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ of $\{\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})(R_i)\}_{i\in S}$.
  Hence the value of $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\circ \bar\Phi$ at the cone point
  is the $P$-filtered colimit of the finite coproducts,
  and hence the  coproduct of the family $\{\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})(R_i)\}_{i\in I}$.

  Now we show part (i).
  The weak equivalences in any model category are saturated,
  i.e., a morphism is a weak equivalence if and only if it becomes an equivalence in
  the localization.
  So the functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is conservative.
  Since this composite is descended from a fully homotopical right Quillen functor
  of model categories, it has a left adjoint by \cite[Theorem 2.1]{mazelgee:adjunctions}.
  We showed above that $u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$
  preserves all colimits.
  The forgetful functor  $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  preserves sifted colimits by \cite[Proposition 3.2.3.1]{lurie:higher_algebra}.
  So the composite $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves sifted colimits.
  In particular, $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves geometric realization,
  i.e., colimits of simplicial objects.
  Since $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is conservative, has a left adjoint
  and preserves geometric realization, it is monadic by the Lurie--Barr--Beck theorem
  \cite[Theorem 4.7.3.5]{lurie:higher_algebra}.


  (ii) We exploit that the $\infty$-category ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  of global spectra is compactly generated,
  hence $\kappa$-presentable, for some regular cardinal $\kappa$.
  The functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is monadic by (i).
  So there is a monad ${\mathcal M}$ on the presentable $\infty$-category
  ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ such that $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is equivalent to $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}})$.
  Since the functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves
  sifted colimits, the underlying endofunctor of ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  of the monad ${\mathcal M}$ preserves sifted colimits.
  So the $\infty$-category of algebras over ${\mathcal M}$,
  and hence also $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$,  is $\kappa$-presentable
  by  \cite[Corollary 6.8]{henry-meadows:monads}.


  (iii) The functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is conservative,
  hence so is the functor $u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\allowbreak\longrightarrow \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$.
  We argued above that the functor $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves all colimits;
  so it is in particular accessible.
  The functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ has a left adjoint,
  so it preserves all limits. Since 
  $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  creates all limits by \cite[Corollary 3.2.2.5]{lurie:higher_algebra},
  we deduce that the functor $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves all limits.
  The $\infty$-category $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is
  presentable by \cite[Corollary 3.2.3.5]{lurie:higher_algebra}.
  Since $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is also presentable by (ii), and $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves all limits and colimits,
  it has both a left adjoint and a right adjoint
  by Lurie's adjoint functor theorem \cite[Corollary 5.5.2.9]{lurie:htt}.

  Since $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is conservative, has a left adjoint,
  and preserves all colimits, $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is monadic
  by the Lurie--Barr--Beck theorem \cite[Theorem 4.7.3.5]{lurie:higher_algebra}.
  Since the functor $u_{\operatorname{gl}}^{\operatorname{op}}\colon (\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}})^{\operatorname{op}}\longrightarrow(\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}))^{\operatorname{op}}$
  is conservative, has a left adjoint and preserves all colimits,
  $u_{\operatorname{gl}}^{\operatorname{op}}$ is monadic by the same theorem; thus $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is comonadic.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- eg-6: body_md -->
An example of a global class that is not a global family is
  the class of compact Lie groups
  isomorphic to a closed subgroup of $U(2)^k$ for some $k\geq 1$;
  this class is even multiplicative, i.e., closed under products.
  It contains the binary tetrahedral group $\tilde A_4$ of order 24,
  because $\tilde A_4$ has a faithful 2-dimensional unitary representation.
  But this class does not contain the alternating group on four letters  $A_4$,
  which is a quotient of $\tilde A_4$.
  Indeed, $A_4$ has no 2-dimensional
  irreducible representations, so every homomorphism $A_4\longrightarrow U(2)^k$ kills
  the commutator subgroup of $A_4$, and can thus not be injective.
<!-- end eg-6 -->
<!-- theorem-24: body_md -->
\label{thm:Sp_F properties}
  Let ${\mathcal F}$ be a global class of compact Lie groups.
  \begin{enumerate}[\em (i)]
  \item The $\infty$-category ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ 
    is stable and compactly generated, and hence presentable.
  \item Every ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence between ${\mathcal F}$-left induced global spectra
    is a global equivalence.
  \item The inclusion ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ has a right adjoint
    $\rho_{\mathcal F}\colon{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$, and for every global spectrum $X$,
    the adjunction counit $\epsilon_X\colon \rho_{\mathcal F}(X)\longrightarrow X$ is an ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence.
  \item Any right adjoint $\rho_{\mathcal F}\colon{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$
    to the inclusion itself has a fully faithful right adjoint.
    So $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ is a recollement of stable $\infty$-categories.
  \item
    The right adjoint $\rho_{\mathcal F}\colon {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ to the inclusion
    is a localization of $\infty$-categories at the class of ${\mathcal F}$-equivalences.
  \item For every ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence $f\colon X\longrightarrow Y$
    and every global spectrum $Z$, the morphism $f\wedge Z\colon X\wedge Z \longrightarrow Y\wedge Z$
    is an ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-24 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
We prove (i) and (ii) together.
  By design, ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ is the full subcategory of ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  generated under colimits by the objects $(\Sigma^\infty_+B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)[k]$
  for all $G\in{\mathcal F}$ and all $k\in{\mathbb Z}$.
  All these generating global spectra are compact objects of ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  by \cite[Theorem 4.4.3 (ii)]{schwede:global},
  so ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ is a compactly generated stable $\infty$-category,
  and hence presentable.
  Since the objects $(\Sigma^\infty_+B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)[k]$
  are compact generators of ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ and represent the functor $\pi_k^G$,
  by \cite[Theorem 4.4.3 (i)]{schwede:global}, every ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence between
  objects in ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ is an equivalence in ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$, i.e., a global equivalence.
  
  (iii)
  By design, ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ is closed under colimits inside ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$.
  So the inclusion ${\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves colimits.
  Since source and target are presentable, the adjoint functor theorem
  \cite[Corollary 5.5.2.9]{lurie:htt} provides a right adjoint
  $\rho_{\mathcal F}\colon{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ to the inclusion.
  We write $\epsilon_X\colon \rho_{\mathcal F}(X)\longrightarrow X$ for the adjunction counit.
  For all $G\in{\mathcal F}$ and all integers $k$,
  the upper horizontal map in the following commutative diagram
  is the adjunction bijection:
  \[ \xymatrix@C=12mm{
      h({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}})((\Sigma^\infty_+B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)[k],\rho_{\mathcal F}(X))\ar[r]^-{(\epsilon_X)_*}_-\cong\ar[d]_\cong
      & h({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}})((\Sigma^\infty_+B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)[k],X)  \ar[d]^\cong\\
      \pi_k^G(\rho_{\mathcal F}(X))\ar[r]_-{(\epsilon_X)_*}&   \pi_k^G(X)
    }
  \]
  The two vertical maps are isomorphisms because $(\Sigma^\infty_+B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)[k]$
  represents the functor $\pi_k^G$, compare \cite[Theorem 4.4.3 (i)]{schwede:global}.
  So the lower horizontal map is an isomorphism, and thus
  $\epsilon_X$ is an ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence, as claimed.
 
  (iv)
  As a right adjoint, $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ preserves limits.
  Since source and target are stable, the functor $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ preserves finite colimits.
  We claim that $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ also preserves infinite sums.
  Indeed, for any family $(X_i)_{i\in I}$
  of global spectra and all $G$ in ${\mathcal F}$, the following diagram commutes:
  \[ \xymatrix{
      \bigoplus_I \pi_k^G(\rho_{\mathcal F}(X_i))\ar[r]^-\cong\ar[d]_\cong &
      \pi_k^G(\bigoplus_I \rho_{\mathcal F}(X_i))\ar[r] &
      \pi_k^G(\rho_{\mathcal F}(\bigoplus_I X_i))\ar[d]^\cong\\
      \bigoplus_I \pi_k^G(X_i)\ar[rr]_-\cong&&
      \pi_k^G(\bigoplus_I  X_i)    }
  \]
  The two vertical maps are isomorphisms by (iii).
  The two horizontal isomorphisms exploit that the functor $\pi_k^G$
  takes coproducts of global spectra to direct sums of abelian groups.
  Since this holds for all $G\in{\mathcal F}$, the colimit exchange morphism
  $\bigoplus_I \rho_{\mathcal F}(X_i)\longrightarrow\rho_{\mathcal F}(\bigoplus_I X_i)$
  is an ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence between objects of ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$,
  and hence a global equivalence by (ii).
  This concludes the proof that $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ preserves arbitrary sums.
  Since $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ preserves finite colimits and sums, it preserves all colimits.
  Since ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ and ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ are presentable, the adjoint functor theorem
  \cite[Corollary 5.5.2.9]{lurie:htt} provides a right adjoint to $\rho_{\mathcal F}$.
  The functor $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ thus has adjoints on both sides. In such cases,
  one adjoint is fully faithful if and only if the other one is.
  Since the left adjoint to $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ is fully faithful, so is its right adjoint.
  
  (v) 
  The commutative square
  \[ \xymatrix{ \rho_{\mathcal F}(X)\ar[r]^-{\rho_{\mathcal F}(f)}\ar[d]_{\epsilon_X} &\rho_{\mathcal F}(Y)\ar[d]^{\epsilon_Y}\\
      X\ar[r]_-f& Y    } \]
  and the fact, proved in (iii), that the adjunction counits are ${\mathcal F}$-equivalences,
  show that a morphism $f$ of global spectra is an ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence if and only if 
  $\rho_{\mathcal F}(f)$ is an ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence.
  Since $\rho_{\mathcal F}(X)$ and $\rho_{\mathcal F}(Y)$ belong to ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$, 
  $\rho_{\mathcal F}(f)$ is moreover an ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence if and only if it is a global equivalence,
  by (ii).
  We can then apply the dual of \cite[Proposition 5.2.7.12]{lurie:htt}
  to the functor $L=\text{incl}\circ \rho_{\mathcal F}\colon{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$, which yields
  the desired universal property of a localization.

  (vi)
  For any group $G$ in ${\mathcal F}$,
  the functor $\operatorname{res}_G^\wedge\colon{\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p^\wedge_G$ is strong symmetric monoidal,
  so $\operatorname{res}_G(f\wedge Z)$ is equivalent in ${\mathcal S} p_G$ to $\operatorname{res}_G(f)\wedge \operatorname{res}_G(Z)$.
  The morphism $\operatorname{res}_G(f)$ is an equivalence in ${\mathcal S} p_G$ because $G\in {\mathcal F}$;
  hence also $\operatorname{res}_G(f\wedge Z)$ is an equivalence. Since this holds for all $G\in{\mathcal F}$,
  the morphism $f\wedge Z$ is an ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- eg-7: body_md -->
\label{eg:Thom_left_induced}
  Let $G$ be a compact Lie group in a global class ${\mathcal F}$.
  Then the functor $\operatorname{res}_G\colon{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p_G$
  has a left adjoint
  \[ G\backslash\!\!\backslash    - \ : \ {\mathcal S} p_G\ \longrightarrow \ {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\ . \]
  This left adjoint takes the suspension $G$-spectrum $\Sigma^\infty_+ G/H$
  to $\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\operatorname{gl}}H$, for example because both represent the functor
  $\pi_0^H\colon h({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}})\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ab}$.
  Since $G$ belongs to the class ${\mathcal F}$, so does its subgroup $H$,
  and thus $G\backslash\!\!\backslash(\Sigma^\infty_+ G/H)\sim\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\operatorname{gl}}H$
  lies in the subcategory ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$.
  Since ${\mathcal S} p_G$ is generated, as a localizing subcategory,
  by the objects $\Sigma^\infty_+ G/H$, the entire image of the left adjoint $G\backslash\!\!\backslash-$
  is contained in the subcategory ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$.
  For example, if $V$ and $W$ are representations of a group $G\in{\mathcal F}$, then the
  global Thom spectrum
  \[ (B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)^{V-W}\ = \ G\backslash\!\!\backslash({\mathbb S}^{V-W}) \]
  of a virtual $G$-representation is ${\mathcal F}$-left induced.
<!-- end eg-7 -->
<!-- prop-14: body_md -->
\label{prop:mult=refl}
  For any global class ${\mathcal F}$, the following two conditions are equivalent.
  \begin{enumerate}[\em (a)]
  \item The global class ${\mathcal F}$ is {\em multiplicative}, i.e., 
   for all compact Lie groups $G$ and $K$ in ${\mathcal F}$, the product $G\times K$
   also belongs to ${\mathcal F}$.
  \item The global class ${\mathcal F}$ is {\em reflexive},
  i.e., the inclusion of the full subcategory spanned by groups in ${\mathcal F}$
  into the category of compact Lie groups and continuous homomorphisms has a left adjoint.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-14 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
(a)$\Longrightarrow$(b)
  We let $K$ be a compact Lie group.
  We let $N$ be the intersection of the kernels of all
  continuous homomorphisms from $K$ to some group in ${\mathcal F}$.
  Then $N$ is a closed normal subgroup of $K$, and we claim
  that the quotient homomorphism $K\longrightarrow K/N$
  is initial among continuous homomorphisms from $K$ to groups in ${\mathcal F}$.

  We must first show that the quotient group $K/N$ indeed belongs to ${\mathcal F}$.
  Since compact Lie groups satisfy the descending chain condition for closed
  subgroups, there are finitely many $N_1,\dots,N_k$ among the relevant closed normal subgroups
  such that $N=N_1\cap \ldots\cap N_k$.
  We choose continuous homomorphisms $\alpha_i\colon K\longrightarrow G_i$
  with kernel $N_i$ and $G_i\in{\mathcal F}$. Then the homomorphism
  \[ (\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k)\ : \ K \ \longrightarrow \ G_1\times \dots\times G_k \]
  has kernel $N_1\cap\dots\cap N_k=N$, so $K/N$ embeds into 
  $G_1\times \dots\times G_k$. Since the class is multiplicative,
  the product $G_1\times \dots\times G_k$ belongs to ${\mathcal F}$, hence so does $K/N$.
  
  Now we can complete the argument. If $\beta\colon K\longrightarrow G$ is any
  continuous homomorphism to a group in ${\mathcal F}$, then $N$ is contained
  in the kernel of $\beta$, so $\beta$ factors uniquely through
  the quotient map $K\longrightarrow K/N$.
  
  (b)$\Longrightarrow$(a)  
  The argument for global families in \cite[page 437f]{schwede:global}
  can be adapted to global classes, as follows.
  For $G, K\in{\mathcal F}$, we let $q\colon G\times K\longrightarrow L$ be an initial continuous
  homomorphism to a group $L$ that belongs to ${\mathcal F}$.
  Then the projections $p_G\colon G\times K\longrightarrow G$ and $p_K\colon G\times K\longrightarrow  K$
  factor as $p_G=i \circ q$ and $p_K=j\circ q$ for unique continuous homomorphisms
  $i\colon L\longrightarrow G$ and $j\colon L\longrightarrow K$.
  The composite
  \[ G\times K \ \xrightarrow{\ q\ }\ L \ \xrightarrow{(i,j)}\ G\times K \]
  is the identity, so $q$ is an isomorphism from $G\times K$ onto a closed
  subgroup of $L$. Since $L$ belongs to ${\mathcal F}$, so does $G\times K$.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- prop-15: body_md -->
\label{prop:reflexive}
  Let ${\mathcal F}$ be a multiplicative, and hence reflexive, global class.
  \begin{enumerate}[\em (i)]
  \item For every compact Lie group $K$,
    every initial continuous homomorphism $p\colon K\longrightarrow u K$
